identity.title: Unsupervised Partner Design Enables Robust Ad-hoc Teamwork

problem.claim: Robust ad-hoc teamwork among agents without fixed partners.

gap.claim: Existing approaches require pre-trained partner populations or manual parameter tuning.

contributions.claim: Introduces Unsupervised Partner Design (UPD), a population-free multi-agent reinforcement learning method that generates and adaptively selects training partners using a learnability criterion.
Extends partner selection to joint partner-environment selection when a procedural level generator is available.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish UPD by generating and selecting partners on the fly without pre-trained partner populations or manual parameter tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that UPD consistently achieves strong performance against population-based and population-free baselines across Level-Based Foraging, Overcooked-AI, and the Overcooked Generalisation Challenge.
In a human-AI user study, the authors report higher returns and ratings of greater adaptivity, greater human-likeness, and less frustration than all evaluated baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: UPD is proposed as a population-free approach for robust ad-hoc teamwork.
It generates partners on the fly and adaptively selects them by learnability, while supporting partner-environment selection with procedural generation.
The authors report strong benchmark performance and more favorable human-study outcomes than evaluated baselines.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links partner diversity to on-the-fly generation and adaptive selection by a learnability criterion.

lessons.interpretation: Training-distribution diversity can be framed as an adaptive selection problem rather than requiring a fixed partner population.
lessons.application: For a multi-agent learning paper, define a measurable learnability or training-value criterion and use it to select procedurally generated partners during training.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when partner generation is unavailable or the selection criterion is not operationally measurable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the learnability criterion, algorithmic details, dataset or study size, metric values, statistical analysis, or baseline identities.
The claimed extension depends on availability of a procedural level generator.
